blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — voriconazole visual adverse effects
stem: A client receiving voriconazole reports new abnormal color perception and photophobia. Which interpretation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: These are recognized voriconazole-associated visual disturbances; if treatment continues beyond 28 days, visual acuity, visual field, and color perception should be monitored.
options.B: These findings indicate a therapeutic improvement in retinal function and are expected to resolve the underlying fungal infection without additional visual assessment.
options.C: These symptoms establish irreversible blindness from voriconazole and mean permanent visual loss should be expected regardless of treatment duration or follow-up findings.
options.D: These findings are unlikely to be medication related because voriconazole does not have clinically important labeled effects on color perception, photophobia, or visual function.

rationale: Current voriconazole labeling states that treatment-related visual disturbances are common and can include abnormal vision, color-vision changes, and photophobia. The label also reports prolonged visual adverse reactions such as optic neuritis and papilledema and directs monitoring of visual acuity, visual field, and color perception if treatment continues beyond 28 days. Therefore A is correct. B and D contradict the labeled adverse-effect profile, while C overstates prognosis because these symptoms do not by themselves establish permanent blindness.
educational_objective: Recognize abnormal vision, color-perception changes, and photophobia as labeled voriconazole adverse effects and monitor visual function if therapy continues beyond 28 days.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.4 Visual Disturbances: if treatment continues beyond 28 days, monitor visual acuity, visual field, and color perception. Adverse Reactions — Visual Disturbances: abnormal vision, color-vision change, and/or photophobia are common treatment-related effects.
source_claim_supported: Voriconazole can cause abnormal vision, color-vision changes, and photophobia; visual function should be monitored when therapy continues beyond 28 days.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: recognize adverse effects; provide medication education; monitor therapy appropriately.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as complete visual-adverse-effect interpretations of comparable length.
Removed the original uniquely-long key cue while preserving the exact >28-day monitoring requirement.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the current May 27, 2026 voriconazole label; options are closely length-matched and no second defensible interpretation remains.
